 # SOTA-pin discipline
 
 # Source: parent-port with split claude-sota infrastructure status from `Z:/claude/rules/sota-pin-discipline.md` @ parent-ccc `feeefdfacb05d83b2ec77fbb4c2da2fb9ca41f5b` [VERIFIED 2026-05-02]. The SOTA-pin discipline and four-stage Wire/Surface/Close/Re-fire loop are parent-derived; claude-sota's `PINS.json` manifest is LOCAL at `Z:/claude-sota-installed/PINS.json`, while repo-local `sota_freshness_sweep` and `sota_pin_audit` remain FORWARD-REF/P3 and parent external-cadence runs are TIER-3 provenance only.
 # Status: protocol codified; repo-local audit infrastructure FORWARD-REF for P3 hooks port.
 
 A SOTA-pin (model SHA, tool version, plugin version, MCP inventory baseline, cited-repo HEAD SHA) is a claim about external state. Without mechanized re-verification, the claim drifts silently — `[VERIFIED 2026-04-25]` becomes `[VERIFIED-but-actually-stale]` within days. The chassis is `PINS.json` (manifest, LOCAL at `Z:/claude-sota-installed/PINS.json`) + `sota_freshness_sweep` script (audit, FORWARD-REF for repo-local; TIER-3 external-cadence provenance currently exists only via parent Z:/claude/scripts/sota_freshness_sweep.py) + `sota_pin_audit` hook (SessionStart consumer, FORWARD-REF for P3).
 
 This rule is the consumer-side discipline parallel to `.claude/rules/audit-action-loop.md`, scoped specifically to SOTA-reference freshness rather than count-claim drift.
 
 ## Pattern signature
 
 - Stage 1 — **Wire**: repo-local `sota_freshness_sweep` script with `--write-jsonl` flag on PostToolUse `Bash(git commit *)` matcher + repo-local `sota_pin_audit` hook on SessionStart group[0]. Status: **FORWARD-REF for P3**. Current coverage: **TIER-3 external-cadence provenance** via parent Z:/claude/scripts/sota_freshness_sweep.py running cross-project (iter-5 confirmed CLEAN), not claude-sota authority.
 - Stage 2 — **Surface**: `.claude/state/sota_pin_audit.jsonl` accumulates drift records; SessionStart `additionalContext` markdown lists drifted categories WARN-only.
 - Stage 3 — **Close**: a /loop fire ships `chore(pins):` commit bumping `PINS.json` (or `tools-pin.txt`) entry with `verified: YYYY-MM-DD` updated.
 - Stage 4 — **Re-fire**: next audit run produces `any_drift: false` for the closed category, confirming closure.
 
 ## When this discipline applies
 
 Whenever a claimed SOTA reference (categories below) doesn't match the actual environment or has gone unverified longer than the per-category freshness window. The first 4 categories are Tier-1 (currently in scope when the audit lands). The 5th category (cited-repo HEADs) is **Tier-3/queued** — schema field defined, but its probe is intentionally OUT of the wired audit per ONE-LOGICAL-UNIT-PER-FIRE.
 
 | Category | Tier | Probe | Pin source | Window |
 |---|---|---|---|---|
 | Model SHAs | Tier-1 | `ollama show --modelfile <tag>` → grep `sha256-...` | `PINS.json:models.*.sha` | 30 days |
 | Tool versions | Tier-1 | `pip show <pkg>` / `<tool> --version` | `tools-pin.txt:KEY` (with `PINS.json:tools.*` for ollama/codex) | 14 days |
 | MCP inventory | Tier-1 | `.mcp.json` server count + `settings.json:disabledMcpjsonServers` length | `PINS.json:mcp.*` | 7 days |
 | Plugin versions | Tier-1 | Read `.claude/plugins/cache/<plugin>/<plugin>/<v>/VERSION` or `plugin.json` | `PINS.json:plugins.*.version` | 7 days |
 | Cited-repo HEADs | **Tier-3/queued** | `gh api /repos/<owner>/<repo>` → `default_branch.commit.sha` | `PINS.json:cited_deps.*.head_sha` | 14 days (once wired) |
 
 Tier-2 (star counts + cpd, axis-3 expiry timers) and Tier-3 (eval scores via WebFetch, citation-anchor resolution) are explicitly OUT of the wired audit — queued for follow-up cycles.
 
 ## How to apply
 
 1. **Detect drift** — read `.claude/state/sota_pin_audit.jsonl` last row OR run the `sota_freshness_sweep` audit interactively after the repo-local script lands. Until then, any cross-project run from Z:/claude/scripts/ is TIER-3 external-cadence provenance only. Drift surfaces as `status: "DRIFT: claimed=... actual=..."` rows.
 
 2. **Pick fix direction** — drift can mean (a) the actual environment changed (e.g. ollama auto-updated): bump `PINS.json` or re-pull pin; or (b) the pin is right but env regressed: fix env (re-install correct version). Read the rationale field in PINS.json + recent CLAUDE.md cycle-attribution lines to decide.
 
 3. **Surgical edit** — single-axis bump: edit ONE `PINS.json` entry (or ONE `tools-pin.txt` line). Update `verified: YYYY-MM-DD`. Commit with `chore(pins): bump <category>.<key> <old>→<new>` prefix for greppable `git log`.

.\docs\w190-hook-3tier-audit.md:43:## Part 3 — SOTA session-preload practice + post-compact budget (PARTIAL — preload practice DOCUMENTED; codex-reviewed budget recipe LOST to FM-17.f)
.\docs\w190-hook-3tier-audit.md:45:**SOTA session-preload practice** (synthesized from `sessionstart-preload-discipline.md` + CCBP `claude-memory.md:34-40`):
.\docs\w190-hook-3tier-audit.md:47:The SOTA preload discipline is **3-layer + progressive-disclosure paths-glob**:

 ## The rule
 
 12. **Upstream-install-priority over sibling-cite-import.** Every architectural primitive MUST follow source-priority order:
     1. **PRIMARY (default)**: install from upstream SOTA repo via official-native-channel per cardinal-rule-6 (npm / cargo / uvx / `/plugin install` / `gh release download` / `docker pull` / `git clone` from canonical https://github.com URL with HEAD-SHA pin)
     2. **SECONDARY (read-only research)**: cite-anchor TIER-1 SOTA pattern at `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/<file>:<line> @ HEAD <SHA>` — immutable cite consumed as RESEARCH input per cardinal-rule-9 read-only research probe exception; NOT install-class
     3. **TERTIARY (last-resort exception)**: cite-import-AMBER from sibling claude-sota per Section 14.5 — permitted ONLY when sota-researcher subagent invocation per cardinal-rule-10 step 4 returns **HONEST-NON-FINDING evidence** demonstrating no upstream parity exists for the primitive
 
     **Cite-import-AMBER is NOT DEFAULT.** Manifest rows MUST satisfy the HONEST-NON-FINDING gate predicate before STAGED → CITE-IMPORT-AMBER promotion (testable):
     - (i) sota-researcher subagent dispatched with explicit upstream-parity-probe scope (probe upstream marketplaces / npm / PyPI / cargo / GitHub repos / Anthropic CC docs / ECC plugin skills / mattpocock-skills / obra-superpowers / anthropic-cookbook for primitive equivalent)
     - (ii) Probe DAG (P1 LICENSE → P2 registry-existence → P3 plugin-namespace → P4 GraphQL stars-and-bands → P5 README/frontmatter → P6 deep audit) per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/agents/sota-researcher.md` returns NO install-class equivalent
     - (iii) HONEST-NON-FINDING return shape per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories`
     - (iv) Manifest row records HNF evidence (sota-researcher dispatch ID + probes + return) in `docs/install-provenance.md` under `effective_tier=TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION` marker per cardinal-rule-1 cite-class lattice (sibling-derived CANNOT be elevated to TIER-1 SOTA per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/citation-discipline.md` rule #8)
 
     **CR-9 install-risk discipline applies at the cite-import fallback layer**: pre-cite-import REVERT check + sibling-bleed defense + version-pin (sibling commit SHA at copy time) + 2-round fix-forward budget. The fallback path is NOT free of CR-9; it inherits ALL CR-9 sub-rules.
 
     **Operational integration with CR-10 + CR-11**: cardinal-rule-10 step 1 ("(a) Install canonical SOTA solution") preempts step (b)/(c)/(d) under CR-12 — research-first-then-install workflow MUST exhaust upstream-install paths BEFORE classifying as cite-adapt OR best-SOTA-recommended OR HONEST-NON-FINDING. Cardinal-rule-11 META-process: every fire involving sibling-cite-import is gated by upstream-parity probe.
 
     ### CR-12 disposition lattice (6 classes — Wave 134 Fire 27 series + W152-F20+ CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL codification)
 
     Beyond the **install-source priority order** (PRIMARY/SECONDARY/TERTIARY) above, every upstream-vs-incumbent relationship falls into ONE of 6 classes. Wave 134 Fire 27 series mapped 5 (classes 1-5 below); W152-F20+ same-arc n=4 evidence promoted CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL as the 6th (per `codification-threshold.md` cycle-321 expected-savings fast-path):
 
     1. **GENUINELY-NEW** — no Anthropic/incumbent parallel exists for the primitive's scope. Disposition: **INSTALL via CR-12 PRIMARY path** (official-native-channel per CR-6). No further audit needed beyond Probe DAG.
 
     2. **DUPLICATE-FUNCTIONALITY** — full parallel exists in Anthropic/eee stack covering same scope and mechanism. Disposition: **REJECT-FOR-FIT** per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/kiss-dry-yagni.md` Must-Never #4 (no duplicate functionality without clear reason).
 
     3. **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** — incumbent and candidate cover overlapping function via DIFFERENT MECHANISMS. Disposition: **CASE-BY-CASE**, typically CITE-PATTERN-ONLY or STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-C mem0 (fact-extraction-based memory) vs eee graphiti (temporal-KG-based) vs mcp-memory (sqlite-vec-based) — same memory layer, different mechanisms.      4. **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** — parallel API surfaces but different scopes; both can coexist. Disposition: **INSTALL as ALTERNATIVE (not PRIMARY)** — primary incumbent retains canonical position. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-A openai-agents-python (vs Anthropic `claude-agent-sdk-python` @ HEAD `b512f256`) — Anthropic SDK = direct CC control plane (PRIMARY); OpenAI SDK = provider-agnostic orchestration (ALTERNATIVE).      5. **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** — core primitive GENUINELY-NEW at the surface level but imports parallel ecosystem at the dependency level. Disposition: **EVALUATE ecosystem cost vs core primitive value** (often CITE-PATTERN-ONLY when ecosystem footprint disproportionate). Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-B langgraph (Pregel BSP graph execution is novel BUT requires `langchain-core>=1.4.0a2` + 6+ langgraph-* sub-package import + LangSmith proprietary recommended). Distinct from PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT (parallel runtime mechanism) and ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT (core primitive new with ecosystem footprint) by requiring: (a) audited object is REFERENCE material not runtime/install artifact, (b) cite-class adoption is the CORRECT primary mode, (c) correct disposition is RATIFICATION of an existing eee rule/practice against the TIER-1-OFFICIAL primary source. VERDICT: APPROVE

Q1 MECHANISM:
Fresh launch and post-compact both use the same documented rule loader: unscoped `.claude/rules/*.md` load at launch; scoped rules load when Claude works with matching files. Anthropic docs say CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.local.md in the cwd ancestor chain load at launch, and path-scoped rules trigger when Claude reads matching files, not on every tool use. CCBP says the same for CLAUDE.md ancestor startup load and descendant lazy load: [claude-memory.md](Z:/repos/deps/claude-code-best-practice-shan/best-practice/claude-memory.md:32) @ `48f2ceb`.

So: `CLAUDE*.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `CLAUDE.local.md` are startup-active. A rule with those in `paths:` can preload on fresh startup because those memory files are read at launch.

`.claude/settings.json` and `.mcp.json` are config files, not documented memory files. They are parsed by the CLI, but I do not see official evidence that parsing them counts as “Claude reads files matching paths” for rule activation. Your observed Read test proves they trigger on explicit Read, not necessarily startup. Treat settings/mcp startup-active as UNKNOWN until tested.

Post-compact: hooks docs say `SessionStart` runs for `compact`, and `InstructionsLoaded` fires at session start and lazy loads. That means startup rule loading re-runs after compact. Prior activated rules may also survive semantically inside the compact summary, but that is not `paths:` activation and will not be fixed by glob edits.

Q2 FIX APPROVAL:
Yes, narrowing away startup-active memory globs is the correct main fix for the measured preload, assuming W196’s 28.2% was measured at fresh or post-compact session start and not mostly compact-summary carryover.

If the real source is post-compact carryover, `paths:` narrowing only helps the rehydrated session’s fresh rule load; it will not remove old rule content already summarized by compaction. Correct fix in that case is: reduce activated rules before compact, prevent hooks from re-injecting broad context, and make compact summaries reference rule names rather than preserving full rule bodies.

Required empirical test:
Add a temporary `InstructionsLoaded` hook logger, then run four sentinel scoped rules:
`paths: ["CLAUDE.md"]`, `[".claude/settings.json"]`, `[".mcp.json"]`, and `["tmp/nonexistent-sentinel"]`, plus one no-path rule. Test fresh startup, explicit Read of settings/mcp, manual `/compact`, and post-compact SessionStart. The logger should record loaded rule path + event source.

Q3 SAFETY:
General safe-narrowing rule:
Keep a glob only if the rule must be available automatically when Claude reads or edits that file class. Strip globs that merely point at governance documents, provenance, or examples. If a rule governs edits to `CLAUDE.md` itself, either keep the startup tax intentionally, or split out a tiny always-loaded/CLAUDE-scoped sentinel that tells the agent to read the heavy rule only for root-memory edits.

Per-class guidance:

- `cardinal-rule-7/11/12`, `sota-pin-discipline`, `audit-action-loop`: do not blindly strip `CLAUDE.md` if the rule genuinely governs CLAUDE edits. Prefer split: tiny root-memory sentinel stays on `CLAUDE*.md`; heavy rule keeps task surfaces like settings, manifests, provenance, agents, plugins.
- `cardinal-rule-8`: already no-path intentional always-load; leave alone unless reducing its body.
- `canonical`, `karpathy-adapted`, `kiss-dry-yagni`: strip `CLAUDE*.md` unless they specifically govern root memory edits. Keep concrete authoring/code surfaces: `scripts/**`, `tools/**`, `tests/**`, `evals/**`, `.claude/hooks/**`, `.claude/agents/**`, `.claude/commands/**`, `.claude/skills/**`.
- `citation-discipline`, `evidence-policy`: keep `docs/**`, `reports/**`, `.claude/agents/**`, `.claude/commands/**`, `.claude/skills/**`, `.claude/hooks/**` where claims are authored. No need for `CLAUDE*.md` unless root-memory claim edits are in scope.
- `port-note-discipline`: keep code/config surfaces where port notes and cite drift happen. Strip `CLAUDE*.md` unless port-note guidance is meant to fire on root memory edits.
- `cmc-*`, `cross-model-consensus`: strip `CLAUDE*.md` unless cross-model workflow edits to root memory are common enough to pay startup tax. Keep `.claude/state/codex_*`, `.claude/agents/**`, `.claude/commands/**`, `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`. Keep `.claude/settings.json` / `.mcp.json` only if the empirical startup test proves they do not preload, or if you intentionally accept their activation when those files are explicitly read.
- `deprecation-discipline`: `.claude/rules/*.md` is broad but not the refuted recursive glob. Keep if the rule must fire when editing any rule file; otherwise narrow to specific deprecation-governed surfaces.

Sources: Anthropic memory/rules docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory. Anthropic hooks docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks. CCBP local memory note: [claude-memory.md](Z:/repos/deps/claude-code-best-practice-shan/best-practice/claude-memory.md:32).
